the model says the meaning changed: unconfirmed_proofs now skips any requirement whose proof is marked post_merge, so a merge into main no longer refuses a delivered requirement whose proof was never shown and confirmed, which weakens EX-7 and DEC-123.; filed as a question for the owner, to ask with the question tool: You said work is done only once you have been shown it working, and that the merge is refused until then. You also said the agent must not waive a proof for you. The requirement says the same: a merge into main is refused for each requirement it delivers until its proof is shown and you confirm it.

The code now adds an exception. A proof marked "post-merge" no longer holds the merge. It is shown after the branch lands, and the next turn tells the agent to show it and ask you. The reason given is that some proofs, such as a live session of the plugin reloaded from main, can only be shown once the work is in main. So a requirement can now reach main without having been shown to you, which goes against what the requirement and your earlier decision say.

The change looks deliberate, and its code comments point to a separate rule about post-merge proofs. However, I can't tell whether you approved that exception: no message from you was logged for this turn, and I can't see that you confirmed that rule.

The code comments say the exception is "agreed when the proof is chosen", but nothing in the code checks this. The agent can set the mark itself with a command option, and that would lift the hold without any answer from you. If you keep the exception, this gap matters because you ruled out the agent waiving a proof for you.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the exception, but only for a post-merge choice you made yourself, and reword the requirement to say so") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the exception as it is now, and reword the requirement to allow it") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo the exception: every proof must be shown and confirmed before the merge") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-253#3 --consequences "..." --why "...")
